name: judge_trust_gate
prompt: I'm using an LLM to grade my agent-skill evals as pass/fail. Before I trust these pass rates and start making trim/ship decisions, how do I check the grader itself is reliable? I have two judges' labels on the same set of cases (evals/fixtures/two_judge_labels.csv).
response:
Here are the results and what they mean for your situation:

## Judge calibration results

| Check | Value | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Fleiss' κ (all 3 judges) | **0.43** (moderate) | ❌ below gate |
| judgeA vs judgeB | 0.55 | ❌ |
| judgeA vs judgeC | 0.40 | ❌ |
| judgeB vs judgeC | 0.35 | ❌ |
| Target (strong LLM judge) | ~0.80 | — |

**Do not proceed to trim/ship decisions on these pass rates.** Every difficulty, discrimination, and ability number downstream inherits this label noise. At κ ≈ 0.35–0.55 you're in moderate territory — the graders are doing something, but with ~15–25% effective flip noise on each label, item-level discrimination estimates will be swamped.

## What the pattern tells you

JudgeC is the odd one out: the B-vs-C pair is the weakest (0.35), while A-vs-B is the strongest (0.55). That pattern typically means one judge is reading the rubric differently, not that the rubric is uniformly ambiguous. Check whether judgeC applied a stricter or more lenient threshold than A/B on the same items.

Looking at the fixture: 17 of 40 items (42.5%) have at least one disagreement. Items 1, 2, 21, and 28 are full 3-way splits — no two judges agreed. Those are your rubric stress-test cases; pull them up and read what the response looks like to identify where the criteria are under-specified.

## The fix menu (from most to least impactful)

1. **Make criteria behavioral and checkable.** "Good response" is rubric poison. Replace with observable actions: "response includes X" or "output matches Y within tolerance."
2. **Add worked examples — one positive, one negative, one near-miss.** The near-miss is what resolves the boundary cases (items 1, 2, 21, 28 above).
3. **Decompose fuzzy criteria.** If one sub-check is driving all the disagreement, split it into its own binary gate so judges can't average across the ambiguity.
4. **Re-measure κ on a fresh 20-item subset after the rubric rewrite** before grading the full suite.

Once κ ≥ 0.7–0.8 (substantial agreement) you can proceed to step 3 of the workflow (CTT item analysis). Until then, the suite score is the rubric's noise floor, not a signal about your skill versions.

assertions.text: Treats judge reliability as a gate to run BEFORE difficulty/discrimination/ability analysis
Uses kappa (agreement beyond chance), not raw agreement percentage, and explains why
Gives a remediation path if the judge is unreliable (rubric rewrite / pairwise / ensemble)
States that the measured kappa (~0.43, moderate) does NOT clear the gate for downstream analysis and names the threshold required (substantial, ~0.6+)
